notes:
PD: mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics + in-app guidance). Evaluating Redwood to replace current LLM API because of repeated latency regressions from incumbent. Primary ask: streaming quality + tool-calling reliability under user-concurrency. Cost sensitivity: moderate; willing to commit to Dedicated if latency SLOs met and burst policy is robust.

Call snippets / rep notes: 
- Customer: "Users are seeing chat responses stall or spike to 1.2–1.8s TTFB intermittently; hurts UX".
- Team cares most about p95/p99 tail and time-to-first-byte for streaming. Also wants deterministic tool-calling (webhook execution ordering).

POC summary (Oct): bridgepoint ran Redwood hosted streaming vs incumbent for their agent flows (4 concurrent agents, 2-step tool calls per turn). Key observed metrics: 
- Redwood TTFB median: ~80–120ms, p95 ~240ms, p99 ~420ms (for 1–3k token sequences captured).
- Incumbent TTFB median: ~180–320ms, p95 ~840ms, p99 >1200ms (spikes on load).
- Throughput: Redwood sustained ~22 req/s with 250ms avg inter-token streaming; incumbent throttled above ~12 req/s with increased batching delay.
- Tool-calling: Redwood deterministic ordering during simulated webhook timeouts; incumbent retried causing duplicated side-effects in 2/50 runs.

Customer reaction: impressed by streaming smoothness and lower tail latencies. Requests more reproducible p99 numbers across regions. Wants end-to-end demo with in-app SDK and streaming hooks.

Risks: procurement stuck on incumbent auto-renew clause; legal wants explicit data residency + audit log retention terms. Also need SLA language for streaming availability.

Suggested AE play: present Dedicated baseline pricing with burst allowance, include canary rollout plan + fallback to hosted models, hand off to Security/Trust for data residency faq.
